export_rights.summary: Microsoft's Trust Center states 'You own your data'. Under the Microsoft DPA, after subscription expiration or termination Customer Data is retained in a limited-function account for 90 days so the customer can extract it; after that the account is disabled and data (including cached/backup copies) is deleted. Business Central additionally documents a full database export for customers with a paid subscription.
export_rights.post_termination_window: 90 days (limited-function account for data extraction, per Microsoft DPA / Trust Center)

covers: entire environment database: all companies, all tables
routes.how: Business Central admin center > select environment > Database > Create Database Export. Provide a file name, a Blob service SAS URL to your own Azure Standard general-purpose v2 storage account (SAS needs Read/Write/Delete/Create on Containers+Objects, minimum 72-hour expiry), and a container name. Export lands as a BACPAC in your storage container; can take minutes to hours depending on database size.
requires: paid Business Central online subscription (not trial)
D365 BACKUP/RESTORE permission set assigned to the exporting user
customer-owned Azure Standard GPv2 storage account (premium storage not supported)
routes.rate_limits: Maximum 10 database exports per environment per month
gotchas: Premium Azure storage accounts are not supported as the export target
Exported BACPAC is encrypted with the storage account's key, not the environment's customer-managed key
Export can take several minutes to several hours depending on database size

covers: sales and purchase documents (invoices, orders, quotes, credit memos)
routes.how: REST API v2.0: GET https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com/v2.0/<environment name>/api/v2.0/companies(<id>)/<resource>. Auth: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 bearer token, permission Financials.ReadWrite.All (basic auth with web service access keys is deprecated for SaaS since 2022 wave 1). OData query options and $metadata supported; attachment resource exposes attachmentContent as a stream.
requires: Microsoft Entra ID app registration with Business Central API permissions
Business Central user permissions on the underlying data
routes.rate_limits: Per user: 6,000 OData requests per 5-minute sliding window (429 beyond); max 5 concurrent requests; 100 total simultaneous processed+queued requests; max page size 20,000 entities per request (413 beyond); 8-minute operation timeout (408); requests exceeding 10 minutes return 504
gotchas: Extending the standard APIs is not supported; custom fields need custom AL API pages
Resources are per-company - iterate the companies collection to cover a multi-company tenant
Attachments map to Incoming Documents (table 130) and hang off specific parent document types

covers: any table reachable through a page or query object (custom and standard)
routes.how: Publish custom OData endpoints: search for the Web Services page > New > object type Page or Query, assign a service name, check Published. Endpoint pattern: <base>/ODataV4/Company('<CompanyName>')/<ServiceName> (SaaS base is the api.businesscentral.dynamics.com ODataV4 endpoint for the environment). SOAP is also available for Page/Codeunit objects.
requires: permission to publish web services and read the underlying object
routes.rate_limits: Same OData operational limits as the standard API: 6,000 requests per 5-minute sliding window per user, 5 concurrent, 20,000 entities max page size, 8-minute timeout
gotchas: Company names in the URL are case-sensitive
Unpublishing a web service marked for All Tenants also unpublishes other web services on the same object

covers: any list, journal, or worksheet page: chart of accounts, customers, vendors, banks, items, G/L entries, customer/vendor/bank/item ledger entries, posting setup, budgets, sales/purchase documents, contacts
routes.how: Open the list page and choose Open in Excel (read-only snapshot of the current view's columns) or Edit in Excel (Excel add-in, can sync changes back). Microsoft's own pre-cancellation guidance is to export the key master and ledger-entry pages this way, company by company.
requires: permission set D365 Excel Export Action, or system permission 6110 'Allow Action Export To Excel'
gotchas: Multi-company environments require exporting each company separately
Only the columns in the current page view are included - add columns before exporting
Subject to Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit; large ledger-entry exports can take several minutes

covers: setup/master/transactional tables chosen into a configuration package (customers, vendors, items, accounts, posting groups, sales/purchase headers and lines, etc.)
financial report definitions (row and column definitions)
routes.how: Configuration Packages page > create/select a package with the wanted tables > export as a compressed .rapidstart file, or export to Excel (one worksheet per table). Financial reports and their row/column definitions export/import as .rapidstart configuration packages. Packages are re-importable, making this the documented restorable-artifact route for setup data.
requires: permissions on the Configuration Packages page and included tables
gotchas: BLOB-type fields cannot be exported or imported via the Excel format
Do not move, change, or delete columns in exported worksheets or they cannot be re-imported

covers: change-log entries (who/what/when, old and new values, for the tables and fields you enabled logging on)
routes.how: Enable Change Log (Change Log Setup), then view Change Log Entries (page 595). Entries are list data, so they export via the generic Open in Excel action; the Data Analysis feature can slice them in-client. Retention is customer-controlled via Retention Policies (date/time filters), not a fixed vendor window.
requires: Change Log must have been enabled beforehand - it only records changes made while active
D365 Excel Export Action permission for the Excel export
gotchas: Only logs the tables/fields explicitly configured for logging
A configured retention policy may already be auto-deleting older entries - check before relying on history depth

preservation_notes.attachments: Attachments/incoming documents live in the database (Incoming Documents, table 130), so the admin-center BACPAC export captures them. Individually they are retrievable via the API v2.0 attachment resource (attachmentContent stream) per parent document. No dedicated bulk attachment-only export is documented; note that configuration-package Excel export cannot carry BLOB fields.
preservation_notes.audit_log: Change Log Entries (page 595) export via the generic Open in Excel list action; also included in the BACPAC database export. No fixed vendor retention is documented - retention is customer-configurable via Retention Policies, which can silently delete older entries.
preservation_notes.config_artifacts: Configuration packages export chosen setup/master tables as re-importable .rapidstart files or Excel workbooks; financial report row/column definitions also export as .rapidstart packages. Per-tenant AL extensions are the main customization artifact, but the consulted docs do not describe downloading extension source from a tenant - verify in-tenant (Extension Management) or with the implementing partner.

notes: All Business Central doc content was read from Microsoft's official MicrosoftDocs GitHub source repositories (dynamics365smb-devitpro-pb and dynamics365smb-docs), which are the published sources of the learn.microsoft.com pages; the corresponding learn URLs mirror the cited paths. Honest unknowns: no bulk attachment-only export is documented; downloading per-tenant AL extension source from a tenant is not covered by consulted docs; report 'Send to' PDF/Word/Excel export exists per the operational-limits doc's report limits (default 500,000 rows / 6h, absolute 10,000,000 rows / 12h) but its exact UI steps were not confirmed from a fetched doc, so it is not listed as a route; the BACPAC's restorability target (e.g. local SQL Server vs. re-import to BC online) is not stated in the consulted export doc. Older per-environment API rate limits (600 req/min production, 300 req/min sandbox) surfaced in search results but the fetched operational-limits doc states the per-user 6,000-per-5-minute limit used here. The 90-day post-termination window comes from the Microsoft DPA / Trust Center (Microsoft-wide online services terms), not a Business Central-specific document.
research_caveats: learn.microsoft.com was blocked by the research environment's egress proxy, so the Business Central documentation was read from Microsoft's MicrosoftDocs GitHub source repositories (dynamics365smb-devitpro-pb and dynamics365smb-docs, the published sources of the learn.microsoft.com pages) rather than the rendered Learn pages.
